thread:
amelia: Heads up — hitting a blocker while onboarding the Ruby sample app. The UI calls a `whoami` style admin endpoint to show the org/user, but the Ruby SDK doesn't expose it. REST curl works fine, Ruby raises NoMethodError.

ryan: ah, which endpoint exactly? `GET /v1/admin/me`?

amelia: yeah. curl: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/me` returns user JSON. Using the gem: `client.admin.me` -> NoMethodError. I grepped the SDK and there's no admin/me binding.

dev-rel-bot: @amelia filed issue #1428 (ruby-sdk): missing admin.me. Link: https://git.redwood/rel/issues/1428 :white_check_mark:

sam: hmm — might be two separate UX problems here. The sample app expects `whoami` at boot and will retry until it gets a 2xx, so if the SDK call errors in a way the app interprets as transient it spins. Are you seeing repeated retries / stuck spinner?

amelia: exact behavior. frontend shows spinner for minutes. In logs the sampleapp keeps calling the onboarding job and each job triggers the gem call which raises, then job is retried by sidekiq. Feels like an infinite retry loop until we patch the gem or switch to REST.

jordan: can you paste the minimal repro from the sampleapp?

amelia: pasted below:

```
# sampleapp/lib/onboard.rb
user = Redwood::Client.new(token: ENV['REDWOOD_TOKEN'])
me = user.admin.me # >> NoMethodError: undefined method `admin' for #<Redwood::Client:0x00007f...>
open_profile(me)
```

ryan: looked at the generated OpenAPI binding — the admin namespace exists in spec, but the Ruby codegen step skipped it because of a name collision with `Admin` constant in the gem (internal). We should either rename or generate a `admin_client` accessor.

sam: short-term workaround: call the REST endpoint directly from Ruby: `HTTP.auth("Bearer #{token}").get("#{base}/v1/admin/me")` and parse JSON. Not ideal but works. Mention it in the sampleapp README?

amelia: doing that for now. Also noticed another subtlety: the gem lowercases header keys when building the request. The on-prem proxy is case-sensitive for some auth plugins and treats `authorization` differently from `Authorization`, causing a 401 in some environments. That makes the retries worse.

jordan: ouch. header casing should be preserved. Do we have tests for proxies / KMS flows?

amelia: not that I could find. I tried with our staging proxy and saw `401` once, then the app rotated tokens and after backoff got a 200. But combined with the missing admin binding it turned into a long tail failure.

dev-rel-bot: triage: label `sdk/ruby`, `bug`, `onboarding` — assigned to @ryan. P0? maybe P1 depending on impact.

ryan: I'll add a compatibility shim in the next patch: expose `client.admin.me` (wrapper around generated AdminClient) and stop normalizing header case in the low-level HTTP layer. Also will add a small integration test that calls `/v1/admin/me` against the staging proxy to catch regressions.

sam: thanks. Could we also add a note to the quickstart that certain admin endpoints might not be in older gem versions and to fallback to REST? Keeps new users from being blocked.

amelia: yes please — saved my day. Also filing a tiny docs PR for sampleapp with the workaround and a one-liner curl fallback.

ryan: ETA: patch branch later today, release cut tomorrow if no surprises. I'll post a follow-up here when it's released.

amelia: awesome — appreciate the quick turnaround :pray:
